userStories.title: Review round 1 fix 001: address reviewer finding
userStories.notes: CRITICAL [docs/adr/0050-gateship-supersedes-garboard-naming.md:53]: US-001 AC5 requires ADR-0050 to record 'every eliminated candidate with its eliminatory reason'. Lines 53-61 record fabricated aesthetic reasons instead of the measured eliminatory evidence recorded in CAM-434 spec.acceptanceCriteria[4]. Nine of ten entries are wrong: keelgate (ADR: 'awkward compound with no clean phonetic or semantic payoff' / ACTUAL: live software product at keelgate.com since 2026-06-01, Keel root already taken in devtools by keel.so and keel.sh, plus the -gate scandal connotation); deckrun (ADR: 'generic-sounding compound' / ACTUAL: live Kubernetes PaaS whose CLI is named deck, plus a homonymous MCP tool); shipset (ADR: 'reads as a noun phrase for a bundle/kit' / ACTUAL: live AI product at shipset.app); gatework (ADR: "'-work' suffix reads as a services/consultancy name" / ACTUAL: Gateworks Corporation, embedded hardware, with a GitHub org: reviewer independently corroborated via https://www.gateworks.com/company/ and https://github.com/gateworks); bowmark (ADR: 'weak metaphor fit' / ACTUAL: Bowmark Capital, a software-focused PE firm, owns the .com); keelward and wayhelm (ADR: suffix cadence / awkward pronunciation / ACTUAL: live businesses owning the .com); gatepath (ADR: 'generic compound' / ACTUAL: a centenarian NGO owning the .com and .org); gaterun (ADR: 'generic compound' / ACTUAL: SERP taken by the Gate River Run, plus an API-gateway namesake on GitHub). Only the helm- family entry matches. This is not a wording nit: it silently converts nine LAYER-4/namespace kills into subjective aesthetic rejections, which destroys the very evidence this ADR exists to preserve and directly undercuts its own central thesis (line 39: layer 4 is eliminatory). A future naming cycle reading this record would conclude layer 4 almost never bites, when in fact it killed nine of the twelve screened candidates. Rewrite lines 53-61 from CAM-434 AC5 verbatim. Related: line 63 also mislabels the Promark collision as 'a live layer-4-adjacent confusion risk' when Promark is a D'Addario percussion brand (1957), a distant category, not an adjacent one.
